_purpose: THE single editable source of every weight in the crowd model. No weights live anywhere else. Each weight carries a plain-language justification. Change a number here, re-run crowd-model/score.py, and the whole calendar re-scores.
_honesty_statement: These are INFORMED ESTIMATES, not validated predictions. There is no ground-truth 2027 attendance to fit against. This must be stated verbatim on the public Methodology page.

bands._note: Final 0-100 score maps to exactly four bands. Never 'safe/unsafe'.

baseline_by_classification._why: The single largest driver of crowd is the religious rank of the day. Amrit Snan draws akhara processions and the widest public; parva days draw devout crowds; ordinary mela days are far lighter.

amrit_snan.why: Royal-bath days concentrate the entire mela's attention and akhara processions onto one date.

parva_snan_major.why: Amavasya / Purnima / major-festival bathing days draw large devout crowds, well below a royal bath.

auspicious_minor.why: Ekadashi and lesser auspicious days draw committed pilgrims but not the general public.

ordinary_mela_day.why: Any day in the mela window still sees baseline pilgrim flow.

day_of_week._why: Weekends let working families and day-trippers from Mumbai/Pune attend, adding a predictable surge on top of the religious baseline.

saturday.why: Full weekend day; strong day-trip and family turnout.

sunday.why: Full weekend day; strong day-trip and family turnout.

friday.why: Leading edge of the weekend; early arrivals.

holiday_coincidence._why: A public holiday on or beside an auspicious day multiplies attendance by freeing working pilgrims.

on_national_or_state_holiday.why: A gazetted holiday coinciding with a bathing day sharply raises turnout.

adjacent_long_weekend.why: A holiday creating a 3-day weekend around the date raises travel-in.

major_festival_coincidence._why: A major Hindu festival (computed from panchang, e.g. Ganesh Chaturthi in Maharashtra) landing on/near a bathing day compounds crowds, especially locally.

on_major_festival.why: Festival + bathing day is a double draw; Ganesh Chaturthi is especially large in Maharashtra.

within_2_days.why: Festival spillover crowd in the days around it.

amrit_snan_clustering._why: Days near a royal bath inherit spillover: pilgrims arrive early or stay on, and infrastructure is already saturated.

within_3_days_of_amrit_snan.why: Direct spillover shoulder of a royal bath.

monsoon_intensity._why: Heavy monsoon weeks modestly DAMPEN discretionary turnout (travel disruption, flooding risk) even as they raise on-ground danger. This is a small, uncertain second-order effect on crowd SIZE. Data-source: data/imd-rainfall-nashik.json (currently a PLACEHOLDER — replace with sourced IMD Nashik weekly normals and re-derive peak weeks from the data, do not assume).

peak_week.why: Peak-rain weeks slightly reduce discretionary/day-trip crowd.

high_week.why: Heavy-rain weeks marginally reduce discretionary crowd.

low_week.why: Drier weeks see slightly higher discretionary turnout.

monsoon_intensity._uncertainty: Sign and size are uncertain. If IMD data or 2015/2025 attendance contradicts this, reduce to 0 or flip. Documented on Methodology page.

travel_accessibility._why: Nashik sits within a day's road trip of two mega-cities (Mumbai ~165 km, Pune ~210 km). This inflates the WEEKEND surge specifically, because day-trips become feasible. Baseline regional pull is already inside the classification baselines. Source: data/source-cities.json.

weekend_daytrip_amplifier.why: On weekends, feasible day-trips from Mumbai/Pune add to the weekend surge.

historical_attendance_note._why: Nashik 2015 and Prayagraj 2025 distributions inform the shape (royal baths dwarf other days; new-moon > ekadashi). They are used to sanity-check the baselines above, NOT as a separate additive term, to keep the model explainable. See UNVERIFIED.md items 14.
